options: A single dimension table that consolidates several small, unrelated, low-cardinality attributes
A dimension table that stores corrupted or unusable data
A fact table with no measures
A dimension that changes its structure every time the ETL runs
questions.explain: A junk dimension is a deliberate catch-all: instead of many separate tiny dimension tables for flags like order status or gift-wrap, one consolidated table holds them all.

questions.q: How are a junk dimension's rows actually constructed?
options: As the Cartesian product of every value in every attribute being combined, with a surrogate key per unique combination
By copying rows directly from the fact table
By randomly sampling values from the source system
By averaging the values of the attributes being combined
questions.explain: Microsoft's own guidance shows this exactly: three order-status values crossed with three delivery-status values produces nine rows, one per combination, in the consolidated Sales Status dimension.

questions.q: What are the three traits that make attributes good candidates for consolidation into a junk dimension?
options: Many of them, few attributes each, and low cardinality (few distinct values)
High cardinality, complex relationships, and frequent schema changes
They must all be numeric measures
They must already exist as separate fact tables
questions.explain: Good candidates are numerous, simple (often a single column), and low-cardinality — flags, indicators, order status, and demographic states are the textbook examples.

questions.q: What happens to the fact table after several flag dimensions are consolidated into one junk dimension?
options: The fact table's several separate foreign keys collapse into a single foreign key pointing at the junk dimension
The fact table loses all of its measures
The fact table must be split into multiple smaller fact tables
Nothing changes on the fact table — only the dimension side changes
questions.explain: Three separate foreign keys (like OrderStatus_FK, DeliveryStatus_FK, GiftWrap_FK) become one (SalesStatus_FK), narrowing the fact table and reducing the join count for reports that filter on any of those flags.

questions.q: Why would it be a bad idea to junk-dimension five attributes that each have ten possible values?
options: The Cartesian product would produce 100,000 rows, which defeats the purpose of a small, simple consolidated table
SQL Server has a hard limit of 10 rows per dimension table
Fact tables cannot reference dimensions with more than 3 columns
Junk dimensions can only combine exactly two attributes
questions.explain: Junk dimensions only work while the combined cardinality stays small — multiplying out attribute value counts can quickly produce a dimension table larger and less useful than the separate tables it was meant to replace.
